clue.text: Random motion of particles when speed is altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of speed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physics note: particles move randomly whenever their speed changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'speed is altered' as one phrase, but only 'speed' is rearranged; 'is' stays put at the end. Pedesis is a rare term, so the clean wordplay is the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedesis is the technical name for Brownian movement, the jittering of tiny particles suspended in a fluid.

clue.text: Excursion — choose to cut both ends off

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the two words is removed

parts.note: to pick is to choose
to nick is to make a small cut

explanation.surface: A choice of outing: cut both ends off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ends off' takes the last letter K off both PICK and NICK, leaving PIC and NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing with a packed meal eaten outdoors is a kind of excursion.

clue.text: Rough end absorbed by outstanding city

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: a debt outstanding is due

indicators.note: rough means roughed up, so the letters of end are disordered

explanation.surface: A rough conclusion swallowed by a splendid city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' turns END into NDE, and 'absorbed by' puts it in DUE. Dundee is a city in eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a Scottish city on the Firth of Tay.

clue.text: A better means of seeing the sights

definitions.meaning: remarkable displays or scenes worth looking at

explanation.surface: Something helps you take in the tourist attractions better.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses improve vision, and the word also means grand public displays or sights.

clue.text: Do exceptionally well in cutting a Victorian adventure novel

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so in goes inside the novel's title

parts.note: She is an 1887 adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: Excelling at editing down an old adventure book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the inserted letters, cutting the title SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel or stand out is to be brilliant at something.

clue.text: Punishment not supported, basically

definitions.meaning: execution by the rope is a form of capital penalty
suspended from above with nothing under the base, as a picture on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a penalty was, at bottom, unjustified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not supported' reads as 'unjustified', but it means dangling with nothing beneath; 'basically' points to the missing support at the base.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by the noose is a punishment, and a thing suspended from above has no support underneath it.

clue.text: Seasonal worker's dance, a groundbreaker, about to get backing

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
a pick is a tool that breaks up ground

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for about runs in reverse

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A seasonal labourer's dance, about an innovator wanting support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaker' looks like an innovator, but it is a literal tool. Hop pickers harvested hops in Kent, traditionally a working holiday for Londoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual labourers once harvested the hop crop each late summer, a classic seasonal job.

clue.text: Shock over bananas

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for shock reads backwards

parts.note: to stun is to shock

explanation.surface: Shock over the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for mad or crazy.

clue.text: A Yardie's ground, supposedly

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Jamaican gangster's patch, allegedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like territory but means ground up. A Yardie is a member of a Jamaican-linked criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses a presumption, much like presumably or supposedly.

clue.text: Shielding us, having disposed of a large sum of cash

indicators.note: disposed of means got rid of, so a letter is removed from the paper's name

parts.note: the setter writes for the Guardian newspaper, so us is the paper itself
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Protecting us after we have spent a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper this crossword appeared in; dropping its second A and adding G gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shielding and protecting are synonyms, both meaning keeping someone safe.

clue.text: Short story about not switching energy

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: switching suggests the letters of the word not change places

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tale about someone who refuses to change their power supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives C (circa) rather than a containment, and 'switching' rearranges the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conte is a French-style brief tale, often with a fantastical or moral element.

clue.text: Computer entry a pundit corrected (time advanced)

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters of the words a pundit are reordered

parts.note: A stands for advanced, as in the British A level (Advanced level exam)

explanation.surface: A commentator's keyed-in record was fixed, with the clock moved forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' turns A PUNDIT into INPUTDA; T and A follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Information fed into a machine is what a computer receives as an entry.

clue.text: One, following destruction of Reims, is close to death

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
next means following, coming after

indicators.note: destruction breaks the letters of the city name apart and reforms them

explanation.surface: Someone, after the wartime ruin of a French city, lies near death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destruction of' makes REMIS from REIMS, a city in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in extreme circumstances, especially at the point of dying.

clue.text: Extremely insensitive

explanation.surface: A curt verdict: someone is terribly tactless.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Extremely' as modifying 'insensitive'; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word intensifies like very; it also describes numbness, a lack of physical feeling.

clue.text: Dicky, given article and box, improvised

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, so off
the is the definite article
to box is to hit, so cuff, a blow with the hand

explanation.surface: A shirt-front, an article and a boxing bout, all made up on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' suggests a detachable shirt front, which goes nicely with cuff, but here it means off colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without preparation is spontaneous, unscripted, ad-libbed.

clue.text: Very early form of cocaine belonging to French?

parts.note: crack is a smokable form of cocaine
of expresses possession, belonging to
Dawn French is a British comedian and actress (The Vicar of Dibley)

explanation.surface: Asks whether a type of cocaine is the property of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the nationality, but it is the comedian's surname, which supplies her first name, DAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means first light, the earliest moment of the day.

clue.text: Revocation of a legacy, one associated with Piedmont organisation

parts.note: a means one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of Piedmont are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone linked to an Italian regional body cancels a bequest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' suggests a body but signals rearranging PIEDMONT, a region of northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, ademption is the cancelling of a bequest because the property no longer exists in the estate.

clue.text: Racer shares coach

parts.note: stock means a company's shares
a railway coach is a car or carriage

explanation.surface: A sprinter divides up a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shares' looks like a verb but is a noun, and 'Racer' is a vehicle, not a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A modified production car raced on oval tracks is a racing vehicle.

clue.text: Here are the ins and outs of a large office

definitions.text: Here are the ins and outs of a large office

parts.words: Here are the ins and outs of a large office
parts.note: the ins and outs are the incoming and outgoing letters and parcels, handled in one room of a large organisation

explanation.surface: Somewhere to learn all the details of a big workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ins and outs' usually means the details, but here it is literal: incoming and outgoing post.
explanation.definitionFit: The department sorting post coming in and going out of a large organisation.

clue.text: Street cred possibly involves a hush-hush manufacturing advantage

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the a goes inside the rearranged letters
possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters of Street cred

explanation.surface: Street credibility might entail a secret commercial edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STREET CRED into TRDESECRET, and 'involves' then takes A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential recipe or process that gives a firm an edge over its competitors.

clue.text: Historian, a big swinger

definitions.meaning: Edward ... wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
a long-armed ape that swings through trees

explanation.surface: A scholar of the past who was a great party animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon was an 18th-century English chronicler of Rome; the ape of the same name brachiates through trees.

clue.text: Run through one's barrier

parts.note: one's read as one is, which the speaker says as I'm
a pale is a fence stake or boundary, as in beyond the pale

explanation.surface: Someone charges through their own fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' looks possessive but stands for 'one is', so I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a sharp point, as with a sword, is to run someone through.

clue.text: Still, a reticent person needs a change of heart

indicators.note: the central letters of the word swap places, a shift at the heart of it

parts.note: a clam is someone who keeps their mouth shut

explanation.surface: A shy person still needs to change their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs a change of heart' moves the L of CLAM past the A, swapping its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and tranquil are synonyms, describing water or weather with no movement.

clue.text: Reverend's mistake: lovey-dovey type is married

parts.note: someone who spoons, that is kisses and cuddles

explanation.surface: A clergyman's error: the soppy romantic has wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend William Spooner of Oxford gave his name to swapping the starts of words, as in 'you have hissed my mystery lectures'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slip of transposing initial sounds is named after the Reverend Spooner, who was famous for it.

clue.text: One and minus one, continuously

indicators.note: minus means take away, so a letter is removed from the words before

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Arithmetic: one plus minus one, on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus' removes A from the letters ONEAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for hours without a break is going without pause, continuously.

clue.text: Diamond tip

definitions.meaning: slang for a gemstone, especially a diamond
to tip is to tilt or sway, to move to and fro

explanation.surface: A hint about gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a diamond a sparkler or a stone; to tilt from side to side is also the word.

clue.text: Old Cicero's untidy file

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the letters of Old Cicero are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Roman orator's records are in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' looks like a document, but it is a line of people; in Britain a crocodile is a column of schoolchildren walking in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a single line of people, and a crocodile is such a line, typically of pupils.

clue.text: Say backing away from offence is a shadowy area

indicators.note: away from signals the letters are removed from the word for offence

parts.note: to take umbrage is to take offence

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation for say runs backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so say

explanation.surface: Stepping back from causing offence leaves a murky zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EG into GE, which 'away from' takes off UMBRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy and optics the umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow.

clue.text: 'Brummie King' breaks shower dish

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the letters go into the middle of the word for shower

parts.note: a shower of rain
Brummie is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself as me
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Birmingham monarch interrupts a downpour, then a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, but here it is the setter's name, so it gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small baking dish, used for souffles or creme brulee.

clue.text: Plea from French criminal

parts.note: de is French for from
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: An appeal from a French lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: In a courtroom the accused's plea is their case answering the charge.
